India’s information technology (IT) spending is projected to reach ₹16.9 trillion in 2027, registering a growth of 10.6% over 2026, driven by rising investments in artificial intelligence (AI), cloud infrastructure, data centres and cybersecurity, according to a forecast released by Gartner on Tuesday.
“India is entering a new phase of technology investment where AI infrastructure and digital sovereignty are becoming strategic priorities,” said D. D. Mishra, VP Analyst at Gartner.
The expansion of global capability centres (GCCs), rising demand for AI-optimised infrastructure and cloud services, and investments in cybersecurity, sovereign capabilities and data modernisation are driving technology spending growth, he said.
“AI is no longer being treated as a standalone technology investment and is becoming a foundational layer for business growth and digital competitiveness,” Mr. Mishra added.
According to Gartner’s forecast, spending on infrastructure as a service (IaaS) is expected to record the highest growth in 2027, surging 40.3% over 2026. Spending on data centre systems is projected to rise 28.4%.
“IaaS continues to experience strong demand across user segments, particularly in sectors such as financial services and government, which require continued expansion of cloud infrastructure to support growing digital needs,” said Naresh Singh, Senior Director Analyst at Gartner.
He attributed the growing investments in data centre infrastructure to favourable government policies and incentives for cloud and AI, alongside significant commitments by data centre providers and global hyperscalers.
“These investments are expanding compute capacity while advancing India’s ambition to become a global hub for AI infrastructure and applications,” Mr. Singh said.
Software spending in India is forecast to touch ₹2.6 trillion in 2027, marking a 19.3% increase over 2026. The growth will be driven by demand for AI-enabled applications, cloud software platforms and business applications.
“AI capabilities are becoming increasingly embedded across enterprise applications, driving demand for software that supports automation, analytics and workflow orchestration,” Mr. Mishra said.
Organisations are also expected to step up investments in cloud-based software as they modernise applications and deploy new digital capabilities.
“As AI adoption matures, demand is shifting toward higher-value consulting, implementation and advisory services. However, the growing adoption of software platforms with embedded AI capabilities, particularly in the midmarket segment, is reshaping demand for traditional services engagements,” he observed.
